newsitem.title: CROATIA: Two killed in Croatia land mine blast.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Croatia land mine blast.

text.p: Two men were killed and a woman was seriously wounded when a land mine exploded in near a village on a former wartime front line in Croatia, the state news agency Hina reported on Sunday.

The fragmentation anti-personnel mine, said to have been planted by separatist Serb forces before their defeat in battle in 1995, went off in a field in Skabrnja, near the Adriatic port of Zadar, on Saturday.

Police in Zadar said the circumstances of the blast were not yet clear, but the three victims were locals. "It is well known the area is mined. We still don't know what they were doing there," a duty officer told Reuters.
Many thousands of landmines and other unexploded ordnance are still strewn along former frontlines in Croatia and Bosnia 18 months after the end of ethnic wars in former Yugoslavia.
